title: SDK ecosystem onboarding rubric and adapter convergence for enterprise streaming/auth
creator: Maya Chen
description: Goal: Create a repeatable intake and prioritization rubric for enterprise SDK/client requests that unifies language support, authentication patterns, and streaming ergonomics. Scope covers: intake form fields, triage rubric, initial adapter design (protocol-level canonical contract + per-language thin wrappers), and a pilot with two enterprise customers. Out-of-scope for this ticket: full SDK implementation across all languages and long-term distribution/packaging decisions.
acceptance_criteria: Published triage rubric (Confluence) with scoring across: customer size, security needs, latency sensitivity, integration complexity, and maintenance cost
Adapter contract proposal reviewed and approved by Eng and DX teams (includes HTTP/WS handshake, reconnect semantics, token rotation guidance)
Pilot onboarding plan and success metrics defined for two enterprise customers
Telemetry/observability checklist for SDK endpoints added to Console roadmap (span-level + token-level cost attribution)

decision_notes: Adapter approach chosen over full polyglot SDK first: build a canonical transport contract (REST + WebSocket handshake) and provide thin language adapters to reduce duplicate maintenance and ensure consistent behavior across runtimes.

Streaming auth model: adopt a dual-mode pattern — long-lived session IDs for stability and short-lived bearer tokens for per-request authorization. Trade-off: more complexity in server to validate session IDs, but reduced token churn and lower tail latency for high-throughput streams.

Backpressure and flow control: standardize on a windowed ack-based approach for SDK wrappers (ack every N tokens or time interval). This simplifies server batching heuristics and provides predictable latency/cost tradeoffs.
Gradual rollout: pilot with Python and Java, then iterate to Go and TypeScript. Rationale: high enterprise demand and existing internal SDK contributors for Python/Java.
Security: require KMS integration for any adapter that persists tokens; security team to own audit checklist. Will flag security_review_required=true.
risks: Increased runtime complexity to support dual-mode auth (session IDs + short-lived tokens)
Potential mismatch between server batching heuristics and per-language adapter flow control leading to higher tail latency
Dependency on ENG-4390 (long-lived session validation service) may delay pilot
metrics_for_success: Pilot onboarding time < 2 weeks for enterprise SEs
Stream reconnect event rate < 0.5% per 1k streams after adapter defaults
No P0 security findings in security review
Customer-reported integration effort score average <= 2 (on 1-5 scale)
